w: Rubber money built this opera house in the middle of the rainforest, and more than 126 years on it still hosts the annual Amazonas Opera Festival and the resident Amazonas Philharmonic Orchestra. Vogue once named it among the world's most beautiful opera houses -- built at the peak of Manaus's rubber-boom wealth.
s: A rubber-boom opera house deep in the rainforest
_facts: Opera house in Manaus, over 126 years old
Home of the Amazonas Opera Festival and Amazonas Philharmonic Orchestra
Named by Vogue among the world's most beautiful opera houses
Built during Manaus's rubber-boom heyday

w: Brazil's fourth-longest bridge spans the Rio Negro just before it meets the Amazon -- yet connects to nothing but the small town of Iranduba, since the highway it was meant to complete was never finished south of the river. A 2018 study found it drove new deforestation: a true bridge to nowhere.
s: The Amazon's only bridge, and a bridge to nowhere
_facts: 3,595m long with a 400m cable-stayed section; Brazil's fourth-longest bridge
Links Manaus to the small town of Iranduba
The only major bridge across the Amazon or its tributaries
A 2018 study found it induced deforestation

w: A single gold-leafed angel Moroni tops this Latter-day Saints temple near the Rio Negro, its walls cut from locally-sourced Branco Paris granite. Brazil's sixth LDS temple, it opened in 2012 after more than 42,000 visitors toured it during a public open house -- an un-Amazonian spire by the riverbank.
s: A Mormon temple's gold spire on the Amazon riverbank
_facts: Sixth Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints temple in Brazil
Dedicated 10 June 2012 by Dieter F. Uchtdorf
Built with locally sourced Branco Paris granite
Over 42,000 visitors attended the public open house

w: The main transport hub for the entire upper Amazon basin, this riverport on the Rio Negro imports beef and exports Brazil nuts, hides and forest products. Tour boats leave from here for the Meeting of the Waters, where the Rio Negro's black current runs alongside the Solimoes's brown one, unmixed, for nine kilometres.
s: The river hub for boats out to the Meeting of the Waters
_facts: Main transport hub for the upper Amazon basin
Located on the Rio Negro
Departure point for boat trips to the Meeting of the Waters
Exports include Brazil nuts, chemicals and forest products

w: Modelled on the Les Halles market in Paris, this ironwork hall had its metal structure fabricated in France and shipped to Manaus, opening in 1883. Two facades face two worlds -- the Rio Negro waterfront, and the street -- and after a 2006-2013 restoration it still trades fruit, spices and fish.
s: A Parisian ironwork market shipped to the Amazon
_facts: Built 1880-1883, modelled on Paris's Les Halles
Metal structure fabricated in Paris, shipped to Manaus
Two distinct facades: river-facing and street-facing
Restored 2006-2013

w: This cast-iron water tank on Belem street has supplied Manaus since 1899, still feeding neighbourhoods over a century later. IPHAN lists it as national historic heritage for its Renaissance-style shell -- masonry wrapped around seven aedicules and seven matching arched windows and doors.
s: An 1899 water tank still supplying the Amazon capital
_facts: Opened 1899, remains operational
Cast-iron interior, masonry exterior in Renaissance style
National historic heritage listing by IPHAN
Seven aedicules and seven arches repeated on each face

w: Facing the Largo de Sao Sebastiao square, one of Manaus's oldest churches opened in 1888 and became a parish in 1912, mixing Gothic and Neoclassical elements typical of the early rubber-cycle years. European stained glass and panels fill the interior, protected as heritage since 1988.
s: One of Manaus's oldest churches, rubber-cycle Gothic
_facts: Inaugurated 1888, became a parish in 1912
Eclectic style mixing Gothic and Neoclassical elements
European stained glass and painted panels inside
Listed Historical Heritage Site since 1988

w: Unveiled in 1900 opposite the Amazon Theatre, this monument marks a single act with outsized consequences for Manaus: the 1866 opening of the Amazon River's ports to foreign trade, the decision that let rubber money and European ambition flood into the city and build almost everything else on this list.
s: The 1900 monument to the decision that built Manaus
_facts: Inaugurated 1900
Commemorates the 1866 opening of Amazon River ports to foreign trade
Located in the Largo de Sao Sebastiao, facing the Amazon Theatre

w: German rubber baron Karl Waldemar Scholz built this mansion and called it Scholz Palace; in 1918, Amazonas governor Pedro de Alcantara Bacellar bought it and renamed it for the river outside. It served as the seat of state government and the governor's residence.
s: A rubber baron's mansion turned governor's palace
_facts: Originally Scholz Palace, built by rubber baron Karl Waldemar Scholz
Purchased 1918 by Amazonas governor Pedro de Alcantara Bacellar, renamed Palacio Rio Negro
Former seat of Amazonas state government and governor's residence

w: Founded in 1871, the oldest public library in Amazonas nearly burned to the ground in a 1945 fire before being rebuilt within two years. Its 1904-1912 building on Rua Barroso holds over 30,000 newspapers dating to 1886, plus a comics collection added after a 2013 restoration.
s: Amazonas's oldest library, rebuilt from the ashes
_facts: Founded 1871, oldest public library in Amazonas
Current building constructed 1904-1912
Nearly destroyed by fire in 1945, rebuilt within two years
Holds over 30,000 newspapers dating to 1886

w: An English firm, Manaos Harbour Limited, built this eclectic brick complex in the 1900s decade as part of its concession to run the city's port. The exposed-brick blocks were prefabricated in England and shipped over -- an echo of early-1900s London -- and named a national historic site in 1987.
s: A slice of Edwardian London, prefabricated for Manaus
_facts: Built early 1900s by English firm Manaos Harbour Limited
Prefabricated exposed-brick blocks imported from England
Part of the Architectural Complex of the Port of Manaus
National historic site since 1987
